name: MLflow (tracking server, SqlAlchemyStore)
category: developer tool (ML experiment tracking, LLM tracing)
param_style: SQLAlchemy 2.0 Core/ORM compiled by the sqlite dialect; ? positional; IN lists expanded per call; connections set PRAGMA case_sensitive_like = true and register a Python percentile() aggregate
schema_source: the store's own alembic migrations run by SqlAlchemyStore (mlflow 3.17.2 from PyPI) on SQLite, dumped with .schema; only the tables the queries use
data_scale: scale 1: 10 experiments, 15k runs (10k in one sweep), 75k params, 75k tags, 60k latest_metrics, 186k metric points (8 runs x 2 keys x 5000 steps, one 6k-point system metric on step 0), 16k dataset inputs; 9k traces with 45k spans (one 5000-span trace), 27k trace tags, 54k request metadata, 7.7k assessments; ~150 MB
visibility_note: 28.6k stars; the most widely deployed open-source experiment tracker; `mlflow server` and `mlflow ui` default to a SQLite backend store (mlflow.db) since 3.x
interest_note: search_runs builds one DISTINCT query with a join per metric/param/tag filter plus a LEFT JOIN for the order-by metric and CASE null/NaN ordering keys, over runs that have no experiment_id index; metric charts downsample with ntile() + row_number() windows; the trace analytics dashboard runs floor()-bucketed GROUP BYs with percentile() aggregates over trace_info and spans.
reach_note: developer tool; SQLite is the default backend for local `mlflow ui` / `mlflow server`

cpu_evidence.summary: search_runs does not scale beyond thousands of runs; even with column pruning still slow above 20k runs in one experiment
search_runs times out once an experiment's runs reach ~50k logged inputs (dataset inputs fetch per page)
log_batch of 1000 metrics takes ~9 s with SqlAlchemyStore (per-metric insert plus latest_metrics maintenance)
get-history-bulk-interval took ~2.5 s for a 100k-point metric, ORM-loading every row before downsampling; moved the sampling into SQL window functions
metrics logged without a step all land on step 0, so the bulk-interval fetch materialises up to 25k rows for that one step
metric history queries scanned every metric of a run; composite index (run_uuid, key, step) added
a 32,843-span trace is loaded eagerly by get_trace (~82 MB payload): UI hangs and the API times out
